We are going to be working on the lotoffice project and there are a couple of bugs:
1. When I click Start Sale it also highlights Build Quote. When I click something else on the site (I forget what it is), it highlights a second one. I don't like that about it.
2. We need to use our best model to figure out our ShedPro 3D mapping to our lot office quote. Right now it seems to be pretty good, maybe really good, but not quite there yet. We don't want to change it too much but if we can get it more accurate, better. If we can have the AI piece of it actually identify the rows and match them to the add-on rows or the op. motion rows that we have in our dataset and in our information, we want to do that. The end goal that we're going for is that someone can come into lot office and they can start a sale. They can sell a building off the lot or they can start the sale. This start sale wizard is a smart wizard: if they select off the lot then it just gives them that. They can start the sale, sell, and build out the options inside lot office. They can start a sale and it will take them through and open the 3D shape configurator and build it out there. Either way that quote lands in quotes is accurate: landing the boat inside the office so that it's super simple to get to a final boat, regardless of which route they take.
The other part of this that I don't think is built out correctly yet is:
- We have that the customer can sign a contract but we should auto-add the signature of the salesperson that is logged in doing the sale. That should just be on every one so that they don't need to sign that every time. Digitally the customer signs it and then it's there.
- We need a place similar to what we did with 360 Kennel, where we can upload a document, a contract, or create a document or contract that would be the contract that they're signing. It would have some of the things so that we can make that contract so that they're also signing a contract with the company, not just the quote that we're sending them. If I build a quote and we have a company contract that goes out with all of our quotes, or if I'm doing a sale and we have that company contract, that all goes out together. The quote gets attached, if you will, to the company contract. When they sign they're signing on the quote, the specific details of the quote, and also the agreement with the company.
Every dealer will be able to set this up for themselves, obviously. If they are part of a manufacturer's network the manufacturer could set up the overarching contractor and then it would swap in the dealer that is making the sale. It would swap in their information where it's pertinent, where the manufacturer could toggle that on and have it so that the dealer must use their agreement.
